A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G-Designer work. Their text, equations, tables, seven figures, and Appendix A support reliable comparison; the appendix is retained despite repagination.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original benchmark evaluations, communication-cost measurements, adversarial-attack results, case studies, and ablations.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original empirical evaluations, and Table 1 additionally includes G-Designer's previously missing results row.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A retain the same task-node construction, variational graph autoencoder, decoding stages, regularization, and optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, GSM8K, MultiArith, SVAMP, AQuA, and HumanEval, with the same case-study and adversarial-attack scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all 17 baseline rows, and the comparator groups in Figures 5–7 are unchanged. Adding G-Designer's own row does not add a baseline.

E3.justification: The metrics, GPT-4 configuration, five-agent main comparisons, three interaction rounds, 40 optimization queries, temperatures, and attack procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 4–7 retain the same task-adaptiveness cases, token-cost analysis, prompt-attack comparison, agent-count sensitivity analysis, and sparsity/anchor ablations.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. The added Table 1 row follows the existing point-estimate format without new run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds G-Designer's missing row: MMLU 84.50, GSM8K 95.07, MultiArith 98.30, SVAMP 91.85, AQuA 79.47, HumanEval 89.90, and average 89.84. The MMLU and HumanEval scores and overall ranking were already stated in v1. This completes numerical reporting under retained settings; baseline scores and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Equations (1)–(17), their mathematical reasoning, and the appendix algorithm are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same MACP and G-Designer contributions and claims about performance, task adaptiveness, token savings, and adversarial robustness.

C2.justification: The explanations of task-dependent topology selection, efficiency, adversarial resilience, and regularization effects are unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the anonymous code-repository link with the GitHub repository yanweiyue/GDesigner. Documented implementation details, hyperparameters, and Appendix A remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 88 references and related-work discussion are retained, with no change to novelty claims or positioning against earlier research.

P1.justification: Running headers change from 'Trovato et al.' to 'Zhang et al.', and the acknowledgment thanking Robert for bagels and explaining color spaces is removed. The scientific narrative and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains G-Designer's row, causing local text reflow. Reference repagination eliminates a nearly empty spillover page, moving the unchanged appendix from page 12 to page 11. All seven figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Supplying G-Designer's missing Table 1 row makes the existing benchmark claims easier to inspect and compare, particularly for scores previously absent from the table. Updated code-access information and template cleanup improve usability. These are useful reporting improvements; the methods, experimental scope, and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
